title.narrative: Syria Joint Response 2022-2023 - implementation ZOA Syria

description.narrative: The Key Objective of Joint ResponseZOA’s overall objective is to improve access to food security, agricultural livelihood opportunities and basic WASH services, to the most vulnerable households and communities. ZOA’s activities contribute to two specific SJR objectives which are to:1.Provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable people with an emphasis on those in areas with high severity of needs.2.Increase the resilience of affected communities by improving access to livelihood opportunities and basic services, especially among the most vulnerable households and communities.The objectives of the SJR follow the Syria HNO and HRP objectives:a) Saving lives; Provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable people with an emphasis on those in areas with high severity of needs.b) Enhancing protection; Enhance the prevention and mitigation of protection risks and respond to protection needs through supporting the protective environment in Syria, by promoting international law, International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Humanc) Increasing resilience and access to services; Increase the resilience of affected communities by improving access to livelihood opportunities and basic services, especially among the most vulnerable households and communities. Activities span over two years (2022-2023)2022:i.MPCA implemented by ZOA in Menbij sub-district, Aleppo governorateii.Distribution of dignity kits for 700 women and girls through the Dorcas community center in Hullok, Jebel Saman, Aleppo governorateiii.Rehabilitation of two water wells, installation of a silent electric generator to a water station, water trucking and installation of household water tanks implemented by EPDC in Al-Hasakeh sub-district, Al-Hasakeh district, Al-Hasakeh governorateiv.Rehabilitation of a well and distribution of food baskets implemented by GOPA-DERD in Tal Hmis sub-district, Quamishli district, Al-Hasakeh governorate.2023:i.Provision of agricultural inputs/support to farmers implemented by ZOA in Menbij sub-district, Aleppo governorateii.Distribution of dignity kits for 700 women and girls through the Dorcas community center in Hullok, Jebel Saman, Aleppo governorateiii.Rehabilitation of an existing water network by EPDC in Al-Hasakeh City, Al-Hasakeh governorate

The target groups for interventions fall under the following vulnerability criteria that prioritizes households with:1. Persons living with disabilities as they lack access to basic services and face difficulties in meeting their basic needs. Many are unable to work due to their disabilities.2. Elderly members who face limitations in accessing basic services due to reduced mobility and health.3. People with chronic illness and injuries since they face difficulties in accessing needed medicine, healthcare, food/nutrition and have limited access to basic services.4. Female headed households who face particular risks due to their gender and situation, including harmful survival strategies such as early marriage, trafficking and sexual abuse and exploitation.5. People facing extreme socio-economic hardship as they may be exposed to extreme forms of deprivation and they and their families are at greater risk of harmful coping strategies, such as child labour and sexual exploitation. Considerations will also be made for households who have lost or had their livelihoods means disrupted due to COVID-19.

comment.narrative: ZOA is expecting 1 change from the planned activities. Any change will be based on needs.

ZOA replaced the distribution of agricultural inputs by the rehabilitation of irrigation canals. This change enabled ZOA to exceed the original targets 3525 individuals to reach 10312.For MPCA, ZOA increased the target to 1334 HHs instead of the planned 705 HHs. In addition, upon beneficiary request and to mitigate the effect of high inflation, ZOA changed the number of rounds by compiling the three rounds into one, equal to 3,150,000 SYP. The sharp increase in exchange rate enabled ZOA and local partners EPDC and GOPA-DERD to implement additional activities based on tangible needs discovered in PDMs and verification exercises that ZOA carried out.Furthermore, ZOA and Dorcas were able to increase the planned target for 2023 (700 dignity kits) to reach 1168.
